Subject: FinServCorp - Redwood evals discovery follow-up

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Summary:
- Primary use case: document summarization + account-level Q&A for customer support workflows.
- Volume: ~200M tokens/month predicted at peak, heavy short-form Q&A during business hours.
- Constraints: PII redaction required, SOC2 + region residency.

What we propose for the evaluation phase:
1) Redwood-hosted eval environment with a 1-week benchmark using your sample dataset (1000 records) + our augmentations.
2) Compare 3 model variants: Redwood-Chat-2 (base), Redwood-Chat-2-quant (4-bit), and a smaller Redwood-Response-1 for cost comparison.
3) Scoring criteria: exact-match + ROUGE for summaries, hallucination-rate tracking (manual spot-checks), latency p95, and per-token cost estimate.

Attached: FinServ_Eval_Plan.xlsx (detailed timeline), prompt_set_v1.jsonl (example prompts + scoring rubric).

Requested next steps:
- Please share a representative sample (1000 rows) in the JSONL format described in the plan.
- Confirm required SOC2 evidence points and any additional security controls for Private deployment evaluation (if needed).
- Book a 30-min onboarding session with our infra engineer (Dev) to get the dataset into the eval harness.

I can schedule the onboarding for early next week — does Tue 3/30 or Wed 3/31 work?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachments:
- FinServ_Eval_Plan.xlsx (application/pdf 35KB)
- prompt_set_v1.jsonl (application/jsonl 12KB)

Hi Samir / Priya / Michael —

Happy to take these. Short answers and recommended setup: 

Priority day-1 metrics (recommended):
- Correctness (primary): token-level exact-match for short answers + edit-distance-aware F1 for longer spans.
- Hallucination rate (primary): measured as % of outputs flagged by automated heuristics + 10% manual spot checks sampled weekly.
- Latency (SLO): p95 token response time under 300ms for short Q&A, baseline throughput of 50 qps for your expected traffic.
- Cost: per-token cost estimate across model variants + estimated monthly spend for your projected volume.

Model recommendations (to compare in the eval):
1) Redwood-Chat-2 (default) — best quality/latency balance for instruction-heavy Q&A.
2) Redwood-Chat-2-4bit — quantized variant for lower cost, slightly higher variance on rare tokens.
3) Redwood-Response-1-small — lower-cost baseline to measure cost-quality tradeoffs.

Benchmark links / prior runs:
- Eval dashboard (redacted sample): https://dashboard.redwood.ai/evals/finserv-sample-2027
- Model perf brief (pdf): https://drive.redwood.ai/reports/redwood-chat-2-performance.pdf

Dataset/schema notes:
- Preferred format: JSONL with one record per line. Required fields: "id" (string), "input" (string), "expected_output" (string). Optional: "metadata" object — we preserve any additional fields but recommend removing PII before upload.
- If you must keep internal metadata fields, include them under a top-level "metadata" map — Redwood eval harness will pass them through.

Scoring criteria (high level):
- Automated: exact-match, ROUGE-L, BLEU where applicable, hallucination heuristics (entity contradictions), and latency profiling.
- Manual: quality rubric for 5-point correctness + contextual appropriateness, evaluated on a stratified sample of 200 records.

Security/ops notes:
- For SOC2-related evidence, we can run the eval inside a Private VPC workspace or provide an encrypted upload to our hosted eval environment.
- We log all eval runs and provide token-level cost breakdowns.

Next steps I propose:
- Samir: share the 1k sample JSONL (remove PII or flag fields you want redacted).
- Dev: will pick a time to onboard your S3 + credentials to the eval harness.

Happy to hop on a quick call with Michael if you want to align on scoring.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Applied ML | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
